reason: Identifies which items are liquidity options sold by the bank: committed lines granted, sight deposits, prepayable loans.
Liquidity outflow and financial impact of a credit line drawdown from contract versus market spread.
Liquidity and financial impact of a savings account closure: large outflow, small margin loss.
Which impact of liquidity options can be hedged (financial, partly) versus only managed by reserves and credit lines.
Pricing the cost of liquidity tools into client contracts; not identification, impact or hedgeability of options, so no selector.
Behavioural adjustment of TSECF flows for liquidity options; no selector squarely covers it.
What the TSECF entries and cumulated cash flow CF record: expected positive and negative flows by date.
Definition of the TSECF as dated expected flows, equity in last bucket, maturity ladder versus structural liquidity.
Cumulates TSECF from a balance sheet into the TSECCF at two dates.
Reads negative TSECF against positive TSECCF: solvency from the cumulated position, not a single date's flow.
Cumulates TSECF with annual interest to get the TSECCF at year 4.
Scope of what a real-balance-sheet TSECF includes (new business, rollover); no selector covers it.
Causes versus sources: which positive amounts belong in the TSECF; not a listed selector.
Cumulates a six-year TSECF table into the TSECCF and finds its most negative point.
Interprets month-4 inflow against a negative cumulated position, not single-date net balance.
Model families (interest rate, credit, behavioural) for adjusting a TSECF; no selector covers it.
Reads solvency from the TSECCF: positive at all times is ideal, negative expected values imply possible insolvency.
Why a positive expected TSECCF does not remove the need for buffers; no selector squarely covers it.
What the TSAA records: quantity in the bank's possession regardless of ownership, and its relation to TSECF flows.
Which securities financing contracts raise the TSAA: possession-driven effect, ownership staying with counterparty.
Purchase of a bond: cumulative TSECCF (outflow, coupons) and TSAA level after 13 months.
Sale of bond: TSCLGC inflow as notional times price plus accrued interest; haircut is a distractor.
Repo cash into the TSCLGC with accrued interest and haircut, and TSAA fall.
Repo effects: coupon stays in TSECF, TSAA falls, cash goes to the TSCLGC.
Reverse repo cash repayment at expiry with haircut, accrued interest and repo rate, recorded in the TSECF.
Effect of a reverse repo on TSLGC versus TSECF and TSAA; transaction-effects table.
Reverse repo versus buy/sellback: cash in the TSECF, coupons and ownership differences, TSAA effect.
Repo versus sell/buyback: TSAA, coupon treatment and cash into the TSCLGC.
Security lending: coupon plus fee entering the TSECF over the contract; which term structures move and by how much.
Security borrowing effects: TSAA up, only the fee in the TSECF, coupon stays with owner.
Which transactions put cash in the TSCLGC: sale, repo, sell/buyback, not reverse repo or lending.
